answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by charging each identity a locked stake and crediting influence only through slow, peer-signed attestations. In a grove of traders, a newcomer posts a bond stamped in umber on the ledger and waits epochs for elders to vouch; fanning one budget into a zephyr of cloned wallets splits that bond into weak, unverified slivers. Since voting weight scales with the square root of stake, ten fakes carry less sway than one committed member, so an attacker pays full capital plus months of waiting for almost no control.
